first.rationale: Current state shows both onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ) declining, suggesting friction in the early user journey is the root problem rather than pricing pressure. memory_31 and memory_86 demonstrated that reducing friction at signup and shortening onboarding both improved activation durably. While promotional_pricing addresses immediate competitive pressure, it risks margin erosion and doesn't solve the underlying engagement problem. Simplifying onboarding targets the measurable decline and aligns with proven levers. Verifying these two memories confirms the magnitude of prior lift and whether conditions have changed. This preserves the option to deploy pricing or other tactics if the simplified flow doesn't reverse the trend, while testing the higher-ROI lever first.
